pages.lesson:
LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 11.3.1 USE OF INTERROGATIVES

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.3: Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: how much more..., when/who/why/what else with peers for example, who else attended the ceremony?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify interrogatives: how, what, when, why, who in sentences correctly
2. use interrogatives how much more..., when/who/why/what else accurately in sentences

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify interrogatives: how, what, when, why, who in sentences correctly
   In simple words: practise until you can identify interrogatives: how, what, when, why, who in sentences correctly. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. use interrogatives how much more..., when/who/why/what else accurately in sentences
   In simple words: practise until you can use interrogatives how much more..., when/who/why/what else accurately in sentences. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives in the examples.
2. Explain Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives.
4. Show that you can: identify interrogatives: how, what, when, why, who in sentences correctly

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives important for a Grade 5 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Construct questions using the pattern: how much more..., when/who/why/what else with peers for example, who else attended the ceremony? how much more sugar was bought?
2. Learning to Learn is inculcated as the learner learns to use interrogatives correctly.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. how much more..., when/who/why/what else with peers for example, who else attended the ceremony?
2. how much more sugar was bought?
3. Why do we ask questions?
4. How do we ask questions?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify interrogatives: how, what, when, why, who in sentences correctly
2. use interrogatives how much more..., when/who/why/what else accurately in sentences

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
